scope: Roles and protecting consumer contracts for the actual build-bridge.py staging list. This is documentation, not source selection, method coverage or full-port acceptance.

groups.why: Let original Node C++ retain its consumed V8-shaped declarations, handles, Maybe results, callback/signature metadata and checks while implementations operate on SpiderMonkey. These declarations supply no V8 heap layout, register ABI or independent Node owner.
protectingContracts: native handle identity and failure-state controls
groups.testLimit: Compilation protects source compatibility. The named native controls exercise selected handle/error operations, not every declared method or fast-call optimization.

groups.why: Store real rooted values, per-context engine state, native fields and process-level engine initialization/entropy/cache identity. Keep Node Environment, argv/options, scheduling and resource policy with original Node owners; use one engine-thread/root admission and retirement path.
protectingContracts: native fields and asynchronous zlib/gunzip consumers
installed CLI and Worker helper retirement
groups.testLimit: The actual native and CLI inventories protect their named construction, field, callback and cleanup paths. Object detail formatting without JavaScript effects and other unselected value operations remain explicit full-family work.

groups.why: Translate actual SpiderMonkey values, byte stores, views, strings and collection values for original Node consumers. Retain real backing-store identity, leases, external-memory credit and deleter ownership rather than copying Node's public Buffer or string policy.
protectingContracts: native handle and backing lifetime controls
asynchronous zlib and actual tarball gunzip
groups.testLimit: These are selected live byte/encoding/collection consumers. Full resizable/shared/detached storage, conversion and collection API variants remain required. trace-codecs-inl.h also contains ordinary value/backing operations; its filename must not be treated as profiling coverage.

groups.why: Use real SpiderMonkey function/script/module compilation, retained source origins and XDR stencils beneath original Node compiler/loaders and their error/retry policy. Bind private cache data to actual engine/bridge inputs and validate it before consumption.
protectingContracts: native parser diagnostics/module metadata/function source locations/hashbang
separate CJS and ESM file gates
groups.testLimit: The frozen case inventories define the qualified parser/loader/cache consumers. They do not prove every cache format/version, loader hook, import phase or VM API. Private SpiderMonkey cache data is not a claim of V8 heap-snapshot compatibility.

groups.why: Connect original Node contextification and native template callbacks to real realms, object construction/brands, property operations, global identifier/declaration lookup, descriptors and exception modes. Engine hooks preserve original SpiderMonkey object/proxy algorithms.
groups.testLimit: VM18 and the application checks protect the reproduced integration failures. Full VM/Proxy/template/RegExp coverage remains required; the source guard rejecting recursive native template creation is not independently qualified by these cases.

groups.why: Expose actual Promise jobs/hooks, embedder continuation data, finalization work and per-realm code-generation callbacks. Original Node remains responsible for nextTick/microtask/async-resource and permission policy; the engine adapter transports its callbacks and values.
protectingContracts: CLI asynchronous drain/natural and explicit exit
groups.testLimit: Named initial async consumers do not qualify complete async_hooks/ALS, finalization, Promise-hook, code-generation-policy or permission variants. General guest WebAssembly remains the agreed later iteration.

groups.why: Connect Node's existing tracing/cleanup methods to SpiderMonkey reachability and supply actual collector limits, external credit and engine census data. This replaces engine-specific collector machinery while preserving Node's native owners and resource retirement.
protectingContracts: VM live and unreachable context cycles
groups.testLimit: External-credit and GC controls are not full heap-space/census/limit/measurement API conformance. The separately reproduced process.memoryUsage RSS ENOSYS remains a libuv/platform gap; no measurement is fabricated to hide it.

groups.why: Supply real saved-frame provenance, source positions, pending exceptions and native inspection of proxies/collections to Node's original error and inspection code. Preserve error ownership and avoid running user getters where the native interface requires inspection without effects.
protectingContracts: native diagnostic ownership and source-coordinate controls
normal REPL and Fetch response inspection
groups.testLimit: Named JavaScript stack/error paths are qualified separately from general inspection APIs. Wasm CallSite/message/stack position branches remain source-identified work for the agreed later guest-Wasm iteration.

groups.why: Reuse portable upstream value serialization while traversing real SpiderMonkey graphs and retaining actual shared-value/conveyor ownership. Keep Node's messaging/transfer policy with original owners.
groups.testLimit: No comprehensive current-artifact serialization/transfer/conveyor runtime acceptance is established by the initial gates. Preserve those required worker/value/engine tests for the complete catalog and family roadmap.

groups.why: Adapt the complete original tracing/extras routines and their argument/result conventions to real engine callbacks and Node's tracing controller. Construct each realm's native extras eagerly so cleanup does not create new callbacks or replace pending errors.
groups.testLimit: Bootstrap/cleanup and plain gc() do not prove complete tracing. GC option-bag, asynchronous and snapshot extension requests are explicit remaining engine-service work; trace protocol output needs its own family acceptance.

groups.why: Feed original portable profile-tree, sampling and heap JSON algorithms with actual owner-thread SpiderMonkey frames, allocation/weak-edge observations and heap graph data. Native producers must stop/join before their callback records and engine owners retire.
groups.testLimit: Shared prerequisite checks do not exercise every active profiler producer or qualify profiles, snapshots, sampling or trace chunks. Direct current-artifact profiling/heap API acceptance remains required. Initial V8 startup-snapshot and Inspector boundaries retain their separate approved follow-ups.

patchGroups.why: Adapt the real Kandelo/Wasm target, static runtime and data types, binary format checks, declared providers and separate host/target toolsets. Keep original Node startup/registration and portable library dependencies; replace unavailable OS/CPU build assumptions rather than public Node algorithms.
patchGroups.testLimit: Build admission and initial startup do not prove all provider APIs, target variants or full OS behavior.

patchGroups.why: Use actual guest thread/stack/entropy/failure services and SpiderMonkey stop, Promise, collector and native callback hooks beneath original Node owners. Preserve FIFO delivery, existing errors/termination, Node-visible failure and producer/resource retirement; keep V8 register/cage machinery out of the target.
protectingContracts: fatal before Environment, after disposal and OOM controls
patchGroups.testLimit: The selected controls do not inject every entropy/allocation failure or qualify all Promise hooks, observers and engine-service variants. Base adaptations are interpreted with the later producer patches; the selected guest-libc abort path supersedes the earlier trap adaptation for this runtime.

patchGroups.why: Represent Node's consumed private names, constructor identities, native properties, buffer ownership and UTF decoding using real engine storage and operations. Preserve SpiderMonkey object/proxy/property ordering and Node callback/field behavior rather than infer identity from public properties or add replacement JavaScript.
protectingContracts: native handle/field/backing and parser lifetime controls
normal REPL and installed JS/TS/HTTP consumers
patchGroups.testLimit: Selected VM and byte consumers do not qualify every private-name, buffer, template, descriptor, Unicode or resizable-store operation. Full-family API and failure variants remain required.

patchGroups.why: Supply real module linking/evaluation/import hooks, compiler stencils, retained source locations and owned parser diagnostic facts. Keep original Node loader/cache/retry/warning/rethrow algorithms; adapt their engine operations and diagnostic correspondence explicitly.
protectingContracts: native parser decision/report ownership/module metadata/function body/hashbang controls
separate CJS and ESM file gates
patchGroups.testLimit: Current cases are not full loader/vm/cache/import-attribute/source-position conformance. Report-copy allocation-failure injection and general guest-Wasm frame metadata require their own qualification.

patchGroups.why: Reuse complete portable V8/Node tracing, profile-tree, heap registry, JSON writer, measurement and sampling routines. Replace engine-private compiler/collector/register inputs with real SpiderMonkey metadata; preserve original public owner and output policy. Optional V8 statistics machinery is distinct from required Node observability.
patchGroups.testLimit: These prerequisites and one real counter do not qualify complete profiling, heap snapshots/sampling, trace output, space metrics or reports. Required engine/observability acceptance remains separate; do not infer it from compilation.

patchGroups.why: Connect actual guest native libraries, target ABI and shared-value leases through original Node owners and the normal dynamic loader. Preserve lazy Amaro loading and its full wrapper; the explicit Undici factory change selects its exact native C parser. FFI CIF/callback and shared-value retirement remain with their original native owners.
protectingContracts: HTTP/HTTPS Fetch and parser callback/GC/Worker retirement
patchGroups.testLimit: Amaro/Undici consumer qualification does not qualify all FFI, addon or shared-conveyor operations. Native addon execution and general guest Wasm retain their agreed follow-ups. Migrate the two temporary native helpers back only after equivalent upstream Wasm qualification.

patchGroups.why: Retain ordinary live startup/interfaces while rejecting the separately agreed V8 startup-snapshot operations and deferred diagnostic-report generation. Keep original Node flags, registration and ordinary error/exit behavior rather than manufacture successful snapshots or report data.
protectingContracts: initial CLI snapshot/report rejection and ordinary error/exit controls
patchGroups.testLimit: Rejection/profile controls qualify the selected initial boundary only. Full snapshots and diagnostic reports remain required follow-up implementation and acceptance, not completed APIs.
